title.narrative: Reflow DGGF TA: validating and upscaling the production of recycled plastic materials for 3D printing in Dehli, India

description.narrative: Globally, more than 270 million tons of plastic waste is produced each year, of which only 5% is re-used but not suitable for further recycling. Each kg of new plastics creates 0.5 kg of CO2 and is expected to make up for 15% of the total global Co2 production by 2050. Existing production methods and industries are damaging the environment rapidly and the negative impacts are mostly visible in fast growing upcoming markets like India. In addition, 3D printing is one of the fastest growing industries, and if 3D printing does not become sustainable it will quickly become a significant source of plastic pollution. Reflow Filament therefore produces flexible and modular 3D printing material (filament) of industrial quality from recycled plastic through its own plastic extrusion technology of which a significant part was developed in India. Its production hubs are located worldwide and aims to improve the entire plastics value chain by using local plastic waste streams to create this product. In order to prepare for future investments and scale-up production of recycled plastics for 3D printing, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provided support to pilot Reflow in India. The pilot project includes the identification of waste streams and supply chain development, scale-up of the production facility and capacity to 1,000 plastic spools based on 95% recycled materials per month, the expansion of the product portfolio, the commercial and technical validation of the first products (Pet) and the development of a founded business plan to attract follow up investments. The project is ongoing and upon successful completion further investments in local production and the supply chain will take place, which may lead to 140 new jobs and sustainable knowledge transfer within the next 5 years, as well as a reduction of plastic waste of 80,000 kg and 45,000 kg of CO2 emissions. Furthermore, Reflow shares its profits in India with a local NGO representing informal waste pickers with the aim to improve their livelihoods and working conditions and to provide their children with access to education to prevent child labour. 180 children of informal waste pickers, of which +120 young girls, already received education through this partnership.
